items.title: Breaking Neutral Bias: Zero-Human-Annotation Fine-Grained Emotion Enrichment via Semantic Drift and Discriminative Re-ranking
items.authors: Qihang Lu(Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications); Wenbing Yang(Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications); Bingsong Bai(Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications); Zihan Sun(Hello Group Inc.); Yueran Hou(Hello Group Inc.); Peilei Jia(Hello Group Inc.); Ya Li(Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications); Jun Gao(Hello Group Inc.); Yingming Gao(Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications)
items.abstract: Large Audio Language Models (LALMs) suffer from Neutral Bias, failing to capture subtle emotional nuances. Existing attempts to address this through text augmentation usually introduce acoustic hallucinations. To address these issues without costly human annotation, we propose a data-centric paradigm: Semantic Drift and Discriminative Re-ranking. Our method employs an LLM to perform multi-dimensional semantic drift, exploring diverse emotional hypotheses beyond neutral baselines. Subsequently, a discriminative judge model filters drifted hypotheses via hard-negative contrastive learning, grounding them in raw acoustic signals. Experiments confirm this hypothesize-and-verify mechanism transforms coarse, neutral-biased labels into precise, acoustically grounded descriptions, enriching fine-grained emotional detail and downstream expressiveness.

title: Methods and data for vocal tract and articulation analysis
header: Monday 28 September 2026 - 14:30-16:30 - Area 14 - 10 - Special Session - Methods and data for vocal tract and articulation analysis

items.title: Acoustic Pharyngometry as an Auditable Anchor for Cross-Speaker EMA Normalization
items.authors: Daniel Friedrichs(Zurich Forensic Science Institute; University of Zurich); Valeriia Vyshnevetska(University of Zurich)
items.abstract: Cross-speaker analyses of electromagnetic articulography (EMA) are confounded by vocal-tract morphology. We present an auditable palate-referenced normalization combining palate-length scaling with a pharyngometry-derived oral landmark anchoring a low-parameter anterior-posterior warp. In German diadochokinetic (DDK) sequences, interspeaker dispersion of multisensor tongue trajectories falls from 31.28 mm to 26.36 mm (scaling) and 26.13 mm (scaling+warp; 16.5% total; most from scaling). Yet leave-one-speaker-out ridge regression does not improve F1/F2 prediction from EMA for DDK or sustained vowels (Hz, Bark, tract-length-normalized). Speaker identification remains high for absolute positions but drops after removing static offsets, indicating residual speaker structure beyond a one-dimensional warp. The method improves geometric comparability but not speaker-independent articulatory-acoustic mapping.

items.title: Vocal Tract Disparity and Potential Implications for Speaker Recognition
items.authors: Tiena Danner(University of Neuchâtel); Valeriia Vyshnevetska( University of Neuchâtel; University of Zurich); Daniel Friedrichs(University of Zurich; Zurich Forensic Science Institute (FOR)); Steven Moran( University of Neuchâtel; University of Zurich)
items.abstract: Perceptual experiments show that listeners recognize female speakers with lower accuracy than male speakers. Automatic speaker recognition systems may also show performance bias against female speakers even when training data sets are gender balanced. The underlying reasons for this discrepancy are unclear. Here, we apply geometric morphometrics to quantify sex-related morphological vocal tract disparity – the extent of shape variation – across both resting and articulatory configurations. We find that male speakers exhibit greater disparity in both resting and articulatory configurations. This morphological idiosyncrasy may in turn generate more discriminable acoustic signatures and offer a biological explanation for higher recognition accuracies for male voices by humans and machines. Our results suggest that innate variation in vocal tract morphology may contribute to performance bias in voice technology and voice perception by human listeners.

items.title: Towards Language-Agnostic Speech Inversion
items.authors: Saba Tabatabaee(University of Maryland College Park); Mark Tiede(Yale University); Suzanne Boyce(University of Cincinnati); Liran Oren(University of Cincinnati); Carol Espy-Wilson(University of Maryland College Park)
items.abstract: Characteristic timing patterns are reflected in the acoustic speech signal, encompassing both vocal tract configuration and acoustic excitation. Previous studies have demonstrated that speech inversion (SI) systems can recover these timing patterns from speech, including oral tract variables (tongue and lip constrictions) and source information such as periodic and aperiodic energies and fundamental frequency. In this study, we develop an SI system that simultaneously estimates oral tract variables and three source information parameters trained on co-recorded American English speech audio and articulatory kinematics and investigate cross-linguistic generalizability by evaluating performance on previously unseen languages. Pearson product-moment correlation scores of 0.83 and 0.74 were achieved on untrained French and Russian respectively, across oral tract variables and source information when comparing estimated data with ground-truth measurements.

items.title: Influence of Vocal Tract Curvature on Speech Acoustics: A Three-Dimensional FEM Analysis
items.authors: Debasish Ray Mohapatra(University of British Columbia); Sidney Fels(University of British Columbia)
items.abstract: Vocal tract curvature influences speech acoustics by shifting formant frequencies and exciting higher-order transverse modes. Nevertheless, many physics-based acoustic models approximate the vocal tract as a straight three-dimensional (3D) tube with a varying cross-sectional area. Although wave propagation in realistic vocal tract geometries has been studied previously, the specific effects of tract curvature on resonance frequencies remain largely unexplored. In this study, a 3D finite element (FE) wave solver is employed to characterize the frequency response of curved vocal tracts up to 14 kHz. The degree of curvature is systematically varied for vocal tracts with both uniform and non-uniform cross-sectional areas. For uniform cross-sections, curvature has a negligible effect on the frequency response. In contrast, for non-uniform cross-sections, curvature excites higher-order transverse modes at high frequencies and produces noticeable formant shifts above 10 kHz.

items.title: Morphoacoustic Modeling of a Dynamic 3D Vocal Tract Using MRI-Constrained Deformations and FEM Acoustics
items.authors: Tharinda Piyadasa(University of Sydney); Michael Proctor(Macquarie University); Tünde Szalay(University of Sydney); Joan Glaunès(Université Paris Cité); Amelia Gully(University of York); Kirrie Ballard(University of Sydney); Emily Kiff(University of York); Naeim Sanaei(Westmead Hospital); Sheryl Foster(University of Sydney; Westmead Hospital); David Waddington(University of Sydney); Craig Jin(University of Sydney)
items.abstract: Understanding the dynamic relationship between 3D vocal tract geometry and speech acoustics is central to speechproduction modelling. Using a constrained Large Deformation Diffeomorphic Metric Mapping (LDDMM) framework, we combine volumetric magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of sustained vocal tract postures with midsagittal real-time MRI of short coarticulated utterances to construct dynamic 3D vocal tract models with time-varying acoustic responses. We demonstrate the approach on an [5ô5] utterance by an Australian English speaker. Five acoustic landmarks define evaluation states in the reference recording, and intermediate meshes are sampled from an rtMRI-parametrised deformation trajectory constrained by midsagittal contours. Finite-element simulations estimate formants from the resulting geometries. Simulated formants are systematically higher, yet track the reference formant trajectories, consistent with hyperarticulation in sustained speech produced under noisy conditions.

items.title: An Approach to Simultaneous Acquisition of Real-Time MRI Video, EEG, and Surface EMG for Articulatory, Brain, and Muscle Activity During Speech Production
items.authors: Jihwan Lee(University of Southern California); Parsa Razmara(University of Southern California); Kevin Huang(University of Southern California); Sean Foley(University of Southern California); Aditya Kommineni(University of Southern California); Haley Hsu(University of Southern California); Woojae Jeong(University of Southern California); Prakash Kumar(University of Southern California); Xuan Shi(University of Southern California); Yoonjeong Lee(University of Southern California); Tiantian Feng(University of Southern California); Takfarinas Medani(University of Southern California); Ye Tian(University of Southern California); Sudarsana Reddy Kadiri(University of Southern California); Krishna Nayak(University of Southern California); Dani Byrd(University of Southern California); Louis Goldstein(University of Southern California); Richard M. Leahy(University of Southern California); Shrikanth Narayanan(University of Southern California)
items.abstract: Speech production is a complex process spanning neural planning, motor control, muscle activation, and articulatory kinematics. While the acoustic speech signal is the most accessible product of the speech production act, it does not directly reveal its causal neurophysiological substrates. We present the first simultaneous acquisition of real-time (dynamic) MRI, EEG, and surface EMG, capturing several key aspects of the speech production chain: brain signals, muscle activations, and articulatory movements. This multimodal acquisition paradigm presents substantial technical challenges, including MRI-induced electromagnetic interference and myogenic artifacts. To mitigate these, we introduce an artifact suppression pipeline tailored to this tri-modal setting. Once fully developed, this framework is poised to offer an unprecedented window into speech neuroscience and insights leading to brain-computer interface advances. The source code and data are available.

items.title: The ArtComp dataset: Articulatory and Acoustic Measurements of Swedish in Speech with Naturally Manipulated Jaw Position
items.authors: Elísabet Eir Cortes(Stockholm University); Lisa Gustavsson(Stockholm University); Ellen Marklund(Stockholm University)
items.abstract: The ArtComp dataset contains time-aligned articulatory and acoustic data from seven native speakers of Central Standard Swedish (CSS). Articulatory data consist of electromagnetic articulography (EMA), electroglottography (EGG) and video. Acoustic data consist of analysis output from high quality audio recordings. The dataset is unique in that it consists of speech where jaw position is perturbed by natural means. Variable vocal effort ranging from soft to shouting was elicited, resulting in variable and exaggerated jaw opening. This type of data enables research targeting adaptive behaviour in the other articulators. Methods used in collecting and post-processing this dataset are described in detail, together with rationale for the methods chosen. A preview of data is given as time-variations and 2D-tracings of sensor data, to visually illustrate processed data.

items.title: Articulatory Analysis of the Mandarin Alveolar–Retroflex Contrast Using Real-Time MRI
items.authors: Qi Wu(University of Tsukuba); Tatsuya Kitamura(Konan University)
items.abstract: This study uses real-time magnetic resonance imaging (rtMRI) to quantify articulatory correlates of the Mandarin alveolar-retroflex contrast. Air-tissue boundaries were extracted using grid-based vocal tract tracking, yielding four measures: normalized constriction location, constriction length, front cavity, and back cavity. Results showed robust retroflex effects on constriction location and front cavity, indicating consistent posterior displacement and systematic anterior cavity expansion. Constriction length effects were less consistent, and back cavity weakly discriminated consonant class. rtMRI frames further revealed frequent tongue-tip-down postures for retroflex tokens. Overall, constriction location and anterior cavity expansion emerged as stable correlates of the contrast, suggesting articulatory targets that may inform pronunciation instruction.

items.title: Tongue-Shape Strategies for Standard Mandarin Retroflex Sibilants: A Preliminary Ultrasound and Unsupervised Clustering Study
items.authors: Zixi Jing(University of Auckland); C. T. Justine Hui(University of Auckland); Karen Huang(University of Auckland); Catherine I. Watson(University of Auckland)
items.abstract: Standard Mandarin retroflex sibilants are often described as non-prototypical retroflexes and may show diverse articulatory realisations. Using tongue ultrasound imaging, we examined five female native speakers from diverse regional backgrounds producing rhyme-matched alveolar-retroflex sibilant minimal pairs in a carrier sentence. Tongue contours were extracted from target frames, represented as 42 points, and aligned by centroid centring. Unsupervised clustering of contour-based shape descriptors yielded six clusters, which were consolidated into three super-strategies (domed, humped, and concave), in a scheme that differs from prior descriptive frameworks. Compositional clustering of super-strategy proportions revealed systematic between-speaker differences. Overall, consistent with prior work, Standard Mandarin retroflex sibilants permit multiple tongue-shape strategies, and speakers show strong, speaker-specific preferences that group them into stable clusters.

title: Grand Special Challenges Poster Showcase
header: Monday 28 September 2026 - 14:30-16:30 - Area 14 - Poster 1 - Grand Special Challenges Poster Showcase

items.title: BEST-RQ-2: Contextualize-Then-Predict, a Two-Step Approach for Self-Supervised Audio Representations
items.authors: Ludovic Tuncay(Université de Toulouse); Étienne Labbé(Université de Toulouse); Thomas Pellegrini(Université de Toulouse)
items.abstract: Self-supervised learning enables audio representations that transfer across domains and tasks. We present BEST-RQ-2, an evolution of BEST-RQ that retains frozen random-projection-based discrete targets while introducing a two-step contextualize-then-predict pretraining scheme. A ViT context encoder processes only the unmasked spectrogram regions, and a lightweight predictor infers targets for the masked regions; the predictor is discarded after pretraining. Replacing the original Conformer encoder with a ViT shifts performance across domains, slightly reducing speech performance while improving music and environmental sounds, with comparable average scores. The main improvement comes from decomposing masked prediction into separate contextualization and prediction stages. On the X-ARES and XARES-LLM benchmarks, BEST-RQ-2 consistently outperforms one-stage baselines in overall transfer while keeping inference compute unchanged. Code and model checkpoints are publicly available.

items.title: WQ-Fusion: Dynamic Gated Attention for Cross-Domain Audio Representation
items.authors: Mingda Lin(Wuhan University); Lei Ding(Wuhan University); Xinyue Zhou(Wuhan University); Tiantian Xiong(Wuhan University); Hanchen Pei(Wuhan University); Gongping Huang(Wuhan University); Hao Zhang(Tencent AI Lab Seattle); Jingdong Chen(Northwestern Polytechnical University); Jacob Benesty(University of Quebec)
items.abstract: While pre-trained models excel in specialized tasks, learning universal representations across diverse acoustic domains remains challenging. To address this, we propose WQ-Fusion, a robust dual-encoder framework for cross-domain audio representation learning. Overcoming the limitations of static concatenation, WQ-Fusion integrates whisper and qwen via an Adaptive Feature Modulation module and a novel element-wise gated attention mechanism. This design enables dynamic feature selection, allowing the model to selectively emphasize relevant acoustic and semantic dimensions. Extensive experiments on the Interspeech 2026 Audio Encoder Capability Challenge (Track A) benchmark demonstrate that by effectively routing heterogeneous information, WQ-Fusion achieves a superior overall score of 0.836, significantly outperforming the strongest single-encoder baseline.

items.title: The Interspeech 2026 Challenge on Transfer of Pragmatic Intent in Speech-to-Speech Translation
items.authors: Nigel G. Ward(University of Texas at El Paso); Marcel de Korte(University of Texas at El Paso); Javier Vazquez(University of Texas at El Paso); Montserrat G. Molina(University of Texas at El Paso); Vanessa Bolado(University of Texas at El Paso); Carol Figueroa(University of Texas at El Paso); Eliya Nachmani(Ben Gurion University); John E. Ortega(Northeastern University); Satoshi Nakamura(Chinese University of Hong Kong)
items.abstract: The Interspeech 2026 challenge task on Transfer of Pragmatic Intent in Speech-to-Speech Translation was motivated by the fact that current speech-to-speech translation systems do not prioritize pragmatic fidelity, and thus do not ideally support people conversing across languages. This paper describes the design, datasets, and evaluation methods for the challenge, and the results for the submissions. We find that even the best system lags human performance by 1.2 points on a 5-point scale, and note strengths and weaknesses of our evaluation methods.

items.title: BiMamba2 Masked Discrete-Unit Prediction for Multilingual Speech Representation for Unsupervised Speech in the Wild Challenge
items.authors: Prakriti Subedi(Howard University); Howard Prioleau(Howard University); Saurav Aryal(Howard University)
items.abstract: We describe our submission to the Unsupervised Speech in the Wild (UPS) Challenge at Interspeech 2026, a bidirectional Mamba-2 (BiMamba2) encoder trained with masked discrete-unit prediction following the HuBERT-style paradigm. The 47.88M-parameter model is trained on 250 hours of speech across 67 languages from the MLCommons Unsupervised People's Speech dataset, with no labeled data. The objective combines masked k-means pseudo-label prediction with language identification supervision and VICReg regularization. On official evaluation, the system achieves an Adjusted Rand Index of 0.735, exceeding four baselines on speaker clustering. Language identification macro-F1 (0.073) and character error rate (0.870) remain below supervised baselines. We analyze a local–official discrepancy in metric scale and checkpoint ranking, highlighting limitations of in-distribution diagnostics for predicting Dynabench probe outcomes.

items.title: Content–Speaker Trade-offs in Continued Self-Supervised Pre-Training Across SSL Paradigms for Multilingual Speech
items.authors: Danner Schlotterbeck(Factored AI); Alessandro Huaman(Factored AI); Juan Gomez(Factored AI)
items.abstract: Continued pre-training (CPT) of self-supervised learning (SSL) models uses domain-specific unlabeled audio to improve downstream performance. However, existing work focuses on contrastive architectures, leaving discrete-unit models underexplored, and rarely examines catastrophic forgetting in multi-task setups. To bridge this gap, we study CPT across three SSL architectures on subsets of the MLCommons Unsupervised People's Speech dataset across three tasks. Re-computing pseudo-labels on target data and resuming masked prediction improves content tasks in label-scarce domains, though gains are high-variance across seeds and data scale. In contrast, comparing discrete-unit and contrastive models reveals a systematic trade-off: CPT degrades speaker-discriminative information in discrete-unit models, an effect contrastive models do not exhibit. These findings highlight undocumented task specialization patterns under CPT, serving as a reference for future domain adaptation.

items.title: Unsupervised Speech in the Wild Challenge: Learning Robust Multilingual Representations
items.authors: Rafael Mosquera Gómez(Factored AI; MLCommons); Juan Felipe Rodríguez(Factored AI); Daniel Galvez(Nvidia); Sarah Luger(MLCommons)
items.abstract: Self-supervised learning (SSL) has achieved remarkable progress in speech representation learning, yet most models are pretrained on comparatively curated corpora with limited acoustic variability. We introduce the Unsupervised Speech in the Wild (UPS) 2026 Challenge, a benchmark designed to evaluate representation learning under large-scale, heterogeneous web audio conditions. Participants are restricted to pre-train from scratch or continue pretraining from a checkpoint using Unsupervised People's Speech (UPS) dataset, comprising over 800,000 hours of publicly licensed web audio, with approximately 522,000 hours of detected speech, and are evaluated on three complementary tasks: language identification, few-shot automatic speech recognition, and speaker clustering.

items.title: Beyond Acoustic Sparsity and Linguistic Bias: A Prompt-Free Paradigm for Mispronunciation Detection and Diagnosis
items.authors: Haopeng Geng(The University of Tokyo); Longfei Yang(The University of Tokyo); Xi Chen(The University of Tokyo); Haitong Sun(The University of Tokyo); Daisuke Saito(The University of Tokyo); Nobuaki Minematsu(The University of Tokyo)
items.abstract: Mispronunciation Detection and Diagnosis (MDD) requires modeling fine-grained acoustic deviations. However, current ASR-derived MDD systems often face inherent limitations. In particular, CTC-based models favor sequence-level alignments that neglect transient mispronunciation cues, while explicit canonical priors bias predictions toward intended targets. To address these bottlenecks, we propose a prompt-free framework decoupling acoustic fidelity from canonical guidance. First, we introduce CROTTC, an acoustic model enforcing monotonic, frame-level alignment to accurately capture pronunciation deviations. Second, we implicitly inject mispronunciation information via the IF strategy under the knowledge transfer principle. Experiments show CROTTC-IF achieves a 71.77% F1-score on L2-ARCTIC and 71.70% F1-score on the Iqra'Eval2 leaderboard. With empirical analysis, we demonstrate that decoupling acoustics from explicit priors provides highly robust MDD.

items.title: IQRA 2026: Interspeech Challenge on Automatic Assessment Pronunciation for Modern Standard Arabic (MSA)
items.authors: Yassine El Kheir(DFKI & Technical University of Berlin); Amit Meghanani(University of Sheffield); Mostafa Shahin(University of New South Wales); Omnia Ibrahim(Alexandria University); Shammur Absar Chowdhury(QCRI); Nada AlMarwani(Taibah University); Youssef Elshahawy(HUMAIN); Ahmed Ali(HUMAIN)
items.abstract: We present the findings of the second edition of the IQRA Interspeech Challenge, a challenge on automatic Mispronunciation Detection and Diagnosis (MDD) for Modern Standard Arabic (MSA). Building on the previous edition, this iteration introduces Iqra_Extra_IS26, a new dataset of authentic human mispronounced speech, complementing the existing training and evaluation resources. Submitted systems employed a diverse range of approaches, spanning CTC-based self-supervised learning models, two-stage fine-tuning strategies, and using large audio-language models. Compared to the first edition, we observe a substantial jump of 0.28 in F1-score, attributable both to novel architectures and modeling strategies proposed by participants and to the additional authentic mispronunciation data made available. These results demonstrate the growing maturity of Arabic MDD research and establish a stronger foundation for future work in Arabic pronunciation assessment.

items.title: A Fusion-Aware Two-Stage Framework for Mispronunciation Detection and Diagnosis in Low-Resource Modern Standard Arabic
items.authors: Jing Yang(Wuhan University); Shuqing Zhang(Wuhan University); Yongyi Deng(Wuhan University); Pan Li(Wuhan University); Ting Dang(University of Melbourne); Gongping Huang(Wuhan University); Jingdong Chen(Northwestern Polytechnical University); Jacob Benesty(University of Quebec)
items.abstract: Accurate phoneme recognition is pivotal for mispronunciation detection and diagnosis (MDD) in modern standard Arabic (MSA), yet remains constrained by data scarcity and the synthetic-real domain gap. This work proposes a two-stage end-to-end framework. It integrates a pre-trained encoder with causal dilated temporal convolutional networks to preserve fine-grained phonetic variations. A hierarchical two-stage strategy first learns general mappings from native/synthetic corpora, then adapts to scarce real learner data to mitigate domain shift without over-correction. Prediction stability is further enhanced via multi-checkpoint ensemble inference with N-gram rescoring. Evaluated on the QuranMB.v2 test set, our system achieves an F1-score of 0.7201, a 63.1% relative improvement over baseline (0.4414). This performance ranks at the top of the IqraEval.2 Challenge, establishing a new state-of-the-art for low-resource MSA in MDD.

items.title: The Interspeech 2026 NeckVibe Challenge: Voice Disorder Detection via Real-World Monitoring of Neck-Surface Vibration
items.authors: Ahmed Yousef(Massachusetts General Hospital; Harvard Medical School); Robert Hillman(Massachusetts General Hospital; Harvard Medical School); Jarrad Van Stan(Massachusetts General Hospital; Harvard Medical School); Matías Zañartu(Universidad Técnica Federico Santa María); Hamzeh Ghasemzadeh(Massachusetts General Hospital; University of Central Florida); Ben Kevelson(Massachusetts General Hospital); Daryush Mehta(Massachusetts General Hospital; Harvard Medical School)
items.abstract: Brief clinic voice disorder assessments miss daily voice use. As an Interspeech 2026 data challenge (NeckVibe), we released a large-scale dataset for vocal hyperfunction (VH) detection, with customized ambulatory hand-crafted voice features. The dataset was recorded during one week of daily activities using a smartphone system that captured neck skin-surface vibration via an accelerometer—including 582 individuals with VH and healthy controls contributing 46,400 monitored hours. For phonotraumatic VH detection, all teams exceeded baseline (AUC = 0.82), with the best test AUC = 0.93. Nonphonotraumatic VH detection was harder: four teams exceeded baseline (AUC = 0.78), with the best AUC = 0.86. Top methods used within-day variability, nonlinear models (XGBoost/CatBoost), speech–singing cues, and feature-to-feature ratios. The challenge yielded new insights into ambulatory VH monitoring for real-world assessment and personalized voice management.

items.title: Temporal Partitioning of Vocal Activity for Detecting Vocal Hyperfunction from Neck-Surface Accelerometer Data
items.authors: Łukasz Łazarski(Samsung R&D Institute); Bartłomiej Eljasiak(Samsung R&D Institute); Szymon Szmajdziński(Samsung R&D Institute); Teresa Makuch(Samsung R&D Institute); Iwan Ryżenkow(Samsung R&D Institute); Anna Plęs(Samsung R&D Institute); Władysław Średniawa(Samsung R&D Institute)
items.abstract: This study presents an ensemble-based framework for classifying Phonotraumatic (PVH) and Non-Phonotraumatic Vocal Hyperfunction (NPVH) using long-term neck-surface accelerometer data. A key factor in enhancing performance was the implementation of temporal data segmentation focused on specific periods of daily vocal activity. Models were developed using the NeckVibe Challenge dataset, comprising 582 individuals, including PVH/NPVH patients and matched healthy controls. On the official challenge test set, our ensemble solution for PVH detection achieved an AUC of 0.925, securing 1st place. Furthermore, our NPVH model reached an AUC of 0.820, significantly surpassing baseline and SOTA benchmarks. These findings underscore the role of feature engineering and temporal optimization in advancing machine learning for ambulatory healthcare. This work was part of the NeckVibe Challenge, organized by the Vocal Hyperfunction Clinical Research Center.

items.title: A Hierarchical Feature Engineering Framework for Automated Classification of Phonotraumatic and Non-Phonotraumatic Vocal Hyperfunction
items.authors: June-Woo Kim(Wonkwang University; GIST); Kangwook Jang(KAIST); Minu Kim(KAIST); Hyunju Lee(GIST)
items.abstract: Ambulatory neck-surface acceleration enables non-invasive monitoring of vocal hyperfunction, yet robust biomarkers for its subtypes remain limited. This study investigates the NeckVibe Challenge dataset to distinguish phonotraumatic (PVH) and non-phonotraumatic (NPVH) from healthy controls. We propose a hierarchical feature engineering framework comprising: (i) static, (ii) dynamic, (iii) ratio-based, (iv) coupling features capturing source filter interactions. While univariate statistical analysis shows strong separability for PVH but limited significance for NPVH, our machine learning pipeline, tailored for high-dimensional feature integration, identifies that coupling features are crucial for both tasks. We achieve an AUC of 0.891 for PVH and 0.728 for NPVH, suggesting that while PVH is near-linearly separable, NPVH discrimination benefits from modeling non-linear feature interactions.

items.title: Attention-Based Multiple Instance Learning with Tabular Stacking for Ambulatory Detection of PVH and NPVH
items.authors: Kiran Yerpude(Seoul National University of Science and Technology; Medisensing); Seung Gyu Jeong(Seoul National University of Science and Technology; Medisensing); Seong-Eun Kim(Seoul National University of Science and Technology; Medisensing)
items.abstract: Phonotraumatic vocal hyperfunction (PVH) and non-phonotraumatic vocal hyperfunction (NPVH) are voice disorders that result from excessive laryngeal muscle activity. The PVH is associated with tissue lesions, while the NPVH refers to functional dysregulation without tissue damage. Ambulatory accelerometers enable the ecological assessment of daily voice behavior, which is noisy and variable. Our method consists of a tabular model at the subject level and a deep multiple instance learning (MIL) model with fixed-lengthwindows of frame-level features. The predictions of these two models are combined via a stacking ensemble method. The tabular model employs CatBoost with day-level features to account for long-term voice behavior, while the MIL model uses a 1D residual network with gated attention pooling to focus on relevant voice segments. The proposed method achieves an official test AUC of 0.891 for PVH (rank 3) and 0.861 for NPVH (rank 1) on the NeckVibe Challenge 2026.

title: Speech Synthesis, Voice Conversion and Audio Generation
header: Monday 28 September 2026 - 14:30-16:30 - Show And Tell 2 - Speech Synthesis, Voice Conversion and Audio Generation

items.title: Coco-VC: Degradation-Robust Streaming Voice Conversion System on the Listener Side
items.authors: Ryo Kato(SoftBank Corp.); Ryutaro Matsunaga(SoftBank Corp.); Toshio Imamura(SoftBank Corp.); Akinori Maeda(SoftBank Corp.); Shuhei Takahara(SoftBank Corp.); Shinnosuke Takamichi(The University of Tokyo; Keio University)
items.abstract: In telephone conversations, speakers lack the means to know how clearly their voice reaches the listener. This degradation in naturalness stems not only from the acoustic and communication environments but also from the speaker's unintelligible timbre. To address this issue, our real-time voice conversion (VC) system, Coco-VC, performs on the listener side. It is built with telephony data augmentation and multi-teacher distillation to extract robust representations. The interactive demonstration showcases a real-time, low-latency streaming VC on a standard laptop, allowing users to seamlessly switch VC settings via an intuitive GUI. Experimental evaluations demonstrate that Coco-VC maintains high quality even for degraded telephony speech compared to existing streaming VC systems.

items.title: Listening to Motion in Space: Vision-Grounded Event-wise Video-to-Audio Generation and Rendering
items.authors: Hyeonwoo Park(Gwangju Institute of Science and Technology); Dayeon Ku(Gwangju Institute of Science and Technology); Hong Kook Kim(Gwangju Institute of Science and Technology; AunionAI Co., Ltd.)
items.abstract: We present VisionSFX, a real-time, vision-grounded video-to-audio (V2A) workflow that generates editable, binaurally-rendered audio from silent video. Conventional V2A systems output a single mono mixture of all sources, which precludes the per-source editing and spatial control routinely required in film post-production, game engines, and AR/VR. End-to-end binaural systems can produce spatialized output but rely on large paired video-binaural training corpora. VisionSFX adopts a training-free route. A vision-language model first decomposes the scene into discrete sound events. Each event is generated independently by a pretrained V2A model within its own temporal window, while ambience is produced separately by a video-agnostic text-to-audio model. The resulting tracks are then spatialized post-hoc using optical-flow centroids with ego-motion correction, monocular depth, and binaural rendering. The pipeline requires no training, fine-tuning, or paired binaural data. Because each source is generated and stored separately, editing one-through re-prompting, repositioning, or timeline injection-leaves all others unchanged. At the booth, visitors upload a video clip and watch a per-source timeline populate within approximately one minute. They then drag sources around in 3D space, rewrite their prompts, or inject new events, with each change reflected on headphones in real time.

items.title: Automatic generation of audio comic from manga images
items.authors: Sota Koshino(Keio University); Shotaro Ueji(Keio University); Shinnosuke Takamichi(Keio University; National Institute of Advanced Industrial Science and Technology); Tomohiko Nakamura(National Institute of Advanced Industrial Science and Technology)
items.abstract: An audio comic is a derivative work based on manga augmented with voice acting. Our system provides a function that (semi-)automatically generates audio comics from manga images. In this paper, we report on the processing pipeline of the system and the objective and subjective evaluation results of the generated audio comics.

items.title: Programmable Speech Synthesis without Computers
items.authors: Takayuki Arai(Sophia University)
items.abstract: We present mechanical speech synthesis devices based on dynamic physical models of the human vocal tract. The models consist of a main vocal tract, with or without nasal branches. The configuration of the main tract is controlled by six sliding blocks inserted from the bottom. To control the position of each block, we tested two cam mechanisms: linear cams and rotating cams. In both cases, the cam profile determines the height of each block. Therefore, for each target phrase, the cam shapes must be redesigned. To make this process “programmable,” we developed a set of interchangeable plates with different profiles, allowing arbitrary cam shapes to be realized by inserting them into the base. This programmable approach allows the synthesis of multiple speech phrases using sliding-block-type vocal-tract models.

items.title: VoiceQualityGUI: A Tool for Word-Level Voice Quality Modifications
items.authors: Harm Lameris(KTH Royal Institute of Technology); Alan Villamil(University of Texas at El Paso); Nigel G. Ward(University of Texas at El Paso)
items.abstract: Voice quality profoundly affects the perceived pragmatic function and suitability of synthesized speech. However investigation has lagged, due to the lack of tools for exploration. To address this need, we have developed a tool that supports modification of creakiness, breathiness, and nasality down to the word level, using an improved version of the VoiceQualityVC voice conversion system. Users can manipulate these properties and experience how such local modulations alter the perceived conversational meanings.

items.title: DsNA(Digital sigNature for Audios): A Unique Method to Fingerprint Audio Files Generated by Text to Speech
items.authors: Vishal Gourav(Oracle Corporation); Phanindra Mankale(Oracle Corporation)
items.abstract: The rapid advancement of text-to-speech (TTS) systems has enabled the large-scale generation of highly natural synthetic speech, raising critical concerns around audio provenance, authenticity, and misuse. In this work, we present DsNA (Digital sigNature for Audios), a lightweight post-generation fingerprinting framework designed to embed verifiable signatures directly into TTS-generated audio. Unlike traditional audio fingerprinting methods that rely on external matching or feature extraction, DsNA introduces a structured embedding mechanism in which a cryptographic signature derived from the audio and metadata is partitioned into shards and interleaved with segmented audio chunks. Preliminary evaluation demonstrates that the proposed method maintains audio fidelity, with no observable degradation in signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) between original and fingerprinted audio. This paper discusses this idea, that enables intrinsic identification of generated speech while preserving signal quality.

items.title: Two Lessons Learned from the SGILE project: Efficient Building and Evaluation of TTS Voices
items.authors: Aidan Pine(National Research Council Canada); Korin Richmond(University of Edinburgh)
items.abstract: In line with the "Speaking Together" theme for Interspeech 2026, our Show & Tell showcases two contributions arising from recent work on the "Speech Generation for Indigenous Language Education" (SGILE) project. Both contributions facilitate building TTS voices for under-resourced languages: 1) the open-source EveryVoice TTS Toolkit can build high-quality voices using constrained amounts of audio data typical for under-resourced languages; 2) we have methodically evaluated speech evaluation techniques with the aim of maximising insights gained while minimising listener effort, especially important when few listeners are available. Our demo takes the form of a web app which combines both these aspects in a single interactive interface: users can experience first-hand a selection of EveryVoice TTS voices through a listening test design that has been little used in the speech synthesis field so far.

items.title: Scalable Audio Scene Generation with the Treble SDK
items.authors: Georg Götz(Treble Technologies); Konstantinos Gkanos(Treble Technologies); Steinar Guðjónsson(Treble Technologies); Daniel Gert Nielsen(Treble Technologies); Jesper Pedersen(Treble Technologies); Finnur Pind(Treble Technologies)
items.abstract: We present the Scene Generator of the Treble SDK, an interactive workflow for constructing realistic audio scenes from room-acoustic simulations, clean source material, and source or receiver definitions. The system supports controlled manual scene design as well as automated bulk generation. A scene is represented as a lightweight recipe containing tracks, source-to-impulse-response mappings, listener configuration, metadata, and target definitions. Audio is rendered only on demand, enabling fast inspection, serialisation, sharing, and scalable dataset generation. In the demonstration, participants build a multi-speaker conversational scene with background noise, visualise it as a timeline and 3D room view, render the scene, inspect targets and transcripts, and then generate many randomised scenes from compact rules.

title: Voice Quality Aspects of Speech
header: Tuesday 29 September 2026 - 09:00-11:00 - Area 2 - Oral 5 - Voice Quality Aspects of Speech

items.title: Tense Voice, Not Falsetto: An F0-specific Physiological Byproduct of Extreme High-Pitch Tone in Kaihui Xiang
items.authors: Yi Zhang(City University of Hong Kong); Aini Li(City University of Hong Kong)
items.abstract: Understanding the interplay between lexical tone and voice quality is crucial for disentangling physiological pitch mechanics from active phonological features, yet the phonatory characteristics of extreme high-pitch tones remain underexplored. In Xiang Chinese, the extreme high-pitch tone (T4) has traditionally been described as falsetto, though recent limited acoustic evidence suggests tense modal voice. To resolve this debate, this study conducts a multidimensional acoustic analysis across the whole tonal inventory of Kaihui Xiang. Results reveal that T4 is produced with tense modal voice, characterized by a flattened lower-frequency spectral tilt, rather than the steep tilt and turbulent noise typical of falsetto. Furthermore, results indicate this tense quality is an F0-specific physiological byproduct, since T4 and T6 exhibit indistinguishable voice qualities where their F0 levels converge.

items.title: The role of phonation type in Chinese Jin tones: a study using acoustic metrics
items.authors: Xiaojing Du(University of Cambridge)
items.abstract: Tonal convergence in Huoji (Han-Xin subgroup, Jin Chinese) compresses f0 space, resulting in overlapping realisations of T1 and T5. Because syllable-final glottal constriction and irregular excitation are common in T5, late-vowel f0 can be weakly defined and tracker-dependent. We ask whether a T1-T5 distinction persists when f0 is compressed and locally unreliable. We compare Praat autocorrelation, YIN, and REAPER under harmonised low-f0 settings, and test whether residual T1-T5 separation is robust across trackers or supported by non-f0 cues. Speech from 17 native speakers was analysed for f0, TBU duration, HNR05, H1*-H2*, and auditory phonation. In MDS, f0-only spaces keep T5 nearest T1 across trackers, whereas adding HNR05 and H1*-H2* expands the space and separates T5 from T1. These results suggest that in Huoji, phonation-sensitive measures complement f0 for modelling T1-T5 distinctions when periodicity weakens near syllable end.

items.title: An investigation of post-stop breathiness in Australian English
items.authors: Thomas Powell-Davies(Australian National University); Rosey Billington(Australian National University)
items.abstract: Stops in English are described as having a voicing contrast. Phonetically, the contrast in onset position is seen as a distinction between short- and long-lag Voice Onset Time (VOT). VOT in onset stops has been studied to some extent in Australian English and other varieties, revealing a range of between-speaker variation. However, the release phase of stops can be more complex than what is able to be captured with VOT alone. Recent work observes periods of breathiness following aspiration for English voiceless stops, akin to observations for voiceless aspirated stops in languages such as Bengali. This study examines post-stop breathiness after onset /p, t, k/ in Australian English wordlist data from Tasmania. Releases with complex transitions in phonation make up over 40% of the data, with variation influenced by (socio-)linguistic factors. The way post-aspiration breathiness is handled has implications for how the stop voicing contrast is treated in English varieties.

items.title: Acoustic correlates of voice quality settings: variation within and between individual speakers
items.authors: Alice Paver(University of Cambridge); Kirsty McDougall(University of Cambridge)
items.abstract: Since perceptual assessments of voice quality (VQ) are sometimes criticised as subjective, there is a tendency for acoustic measures to be treated as objective correlates of articulatory settings. Most acoustic studies generalise across speakers, despite VQ being highly speaker-specific; apparent effects may therefore reflect inter-speaker variation. Acoustic correlates of supralaryngeal VQ also remain underexplored. This study models group-level effects and speaker x quality interactions across multiple measures (CPP, spectral tilt, HNR, long-term formants) for diverse laryngeal and supralaryngeal settings. Group results showed increased spectral tilt measures for both breathy and nasal voice, as well as increased formant frequencies for breathy VQ. However, significant variation was found for individual speakers. These findings challenge assumptions concerning acoustic correlates of VQ and have implications for forensic phonetics and related fields.

items.title: Phonetic evidence for contrastive voicing in Nakanamanga coronal plosives
items.authors: Shubo Li(Australian National University)
items.abstract: For Nakanamanga, an understudied Oceanic language of Vanuatu, it has long been debated whether there is one or two coronal plosive phonemes. This uncertainty has affected historical reconstructions and the understanding of language relationships in the region. However, previous descriptive work has been limited in scope. Recent phonological analyses of Nakanamanga varieties argue for two contrastive phonemes, with voicing as part of the distinction, but acoustic evidence has not been examined. Based on data for the Tongoa variety, proposed to have a voiceless dental /t̪/ and a voiced prenasalised postalveolar /ⁿd/, this study investigates their phonetic realisation, VOT, and closure duration. Results show that /t̪/ is consistently voiceless, with positive VOT and shorter closure, while /ⁿd/ is reliably voiced, prenasalised, with negative VOT and longer closure; the nasal-to-oral closure ratio is 1.88:1. These findings provide clear acoustic support for a /t̪-ⁿd/ contrast in Nakanamanga.

items.title: A Corpus-Based Study of Creaky Voice Production in English and Mandarin
items.authors: Meixian Li(Hong Kong PolyU); Yao Yao(Hong Kong PolyU); Charles Chang(Hong Kong CityU)
items.abstract: Creaky voice has been extensively examined across varieties of English, but cross-linguistic sociophonetic research on it remains limited. This study presents an acoustic investigation of creaky voice production in Mandarin Chinese and US English, using read-speech corpora comprising 66 Mandarin speakers (34F) and 61 English speakers (28F). Audios were processed via a pipeline of segmentation, annotation, cleaning, and acoustic analysis. 5,874 vowel tokens were measured for F0, H1–H2c, HNR35, and CPP over the 70% mid-portion. Linear mixed-effects analyses revealed men produced creakier speech than women in both languages. Findings contradict the notion that creaky voice is predominantly a feature of young women’s speech in US English but align with findings of more creakiness in men’s speech. We discuss the Mandarin results in relation to recent work on Mandarin listeners’ social perception of creaky voice.

title: Speaker Verification and Anti-Spoofing
header: Tuesday 29 September 2026 - 09:00-11:00 - Area 4 - Oral 4 - Speaker Verification and Anti-Spoofing

items.title: RAT: Reference-Augmented Training for ASV Anti-Spoofing
items.authors: Vojtěch Staněk(Brno University of Technology); Anton Firc(Brno University of Technology); Jakub Reš(Brno University of Technology); Kamil Malinka(Brno University of Technology)
items.abstract: We introduce a spoofing countermeasure architecture conditioned on speaker-reference recordings, but observe that it converges to a solution that effectively ignores the reference during inference. Surprisingly, training with a reference channel induces invariance that improves deepfake detection, even when the reference is absent or mismatched during inference. Based on this observation, we propose a Reference-Augmented Training (RAT) strategy. RAT yields improved detection performance compared to single-utterance baselines, even when the reference recording is replaced with a zero vector at inference. Through rigorous analysis, we demonstrate that the optimization process rapidly diminishes the reference contributions, leading to inference largely independent of the reference channel. Using RAT, we achieve state-of-the-art 2.57% EER and 0.074 minDCF on the ASVspoof 5 benchmark with a single detector, surpassing even large ensemble systems.

items.title: SpAArSIST: Sparsified AASIST for Efficient and Reliable Anti-Spoofing
items.authors: Anton Firc(Brno University of Technology); Vojtěch Staněk(Brno University of Technology); Zbyněk Lička(Brno University of Technology); Kamil Malinka(Brno University of Technology); Martin Perešíni(Brno University of Technology)
items.abstract: We present SpAArSIST, a deployment-oriented refinement of the widely used AASIST graph pooling backend for self-supervised learning (SSL) based anti-spoofing. Motivated by redundant operations in public implementations, we replace learned pooling and stack-node attention with explicit, lightweight choices: separate train and inference graph pooling ratios (ktr, kinf), magnitude-based node scoring, and mean aggregation of graph nodes. The best overall configuration (rank 1) cuts backend compute by 20.7% (195.045M → 154.706M MACs) and model size by 4.1% (611.8k → 586.4k params), while improving out-of-domain robustness on In-the-Wild to 2.82% EER and 0.078 minDCF (from 4.64% and 0.133) and remaining competitive on ASVspoof 5. We further provide a composite selection score that summarizes accuracy, calibration, and compute to support balanced deployment-oriented model choice.

items.title: Linguistic Bias Mitigation for Spoofing Detection via Gradient Reversal and A Variational Information Bottleneck
items.authors: Anh-Tuan DAO(LIA; Avignon University); Driss Matrouf(LIA; Avignon University); Mickael Rouvier(LIA; Avignon University); Nicholas Evans(EURECOM)
items.abstract: Rapid advancements in generative speech technology have compromised the reliability of voice biometrics. While current spoofing detectors excel when assessed under in-domain conditions, generalisation to out-of-domain settings is often poor. We show that this can be due to linguistic bias. A reliance on linguistic cues observed in training data can then compromise robustness to cross-data. We propose a linguistic-invariant spoofing detection framework utilizing teacher-student adver-sarial learning. The linguistic-aware teacher model, pre-trained on linguistic content of an external dataset, guides the student detector via gradient reversal to minimize the linguistic information. To prevent the inadvertent removal of non-linguistic cues, we incorporate a Variational Information Bottleneck to enable suppression of principal cues. Across nine DF Arena datasets, our method achieves up to a 36.2% relative reduction in the EER compare to the baseline.

items.title: Spectral Masking and Interpolation Attack (SMIA): A Black-box Adversarial Attack against Voice Authentication and Anti-Spoofing Systems
items.authors: Kamel Kamel(Deakin University); Hridoy Sankar Dutta(Deakin University); Keshav Sood(Deakin University); Sunil Aryal(Deakin University)
items.abstract: Voice Authentication Systems (VASs) are deeply integrated into high-security sectors, yet remain vulnerable to deepfake and adversarial spoofing attacks. While anti-spoofing countermeasures (CMs) exist to mitigate these risks, many rely on static detection models that can be bypassed by novel adversarial methods, leaving a critical security gap. We propose the Spectral Masking and Interpolation Attack (SMIA), a black-box adversarial method that strategically manipulates inaudible frequency regions of AI-generated audio to deceive both VAS and CMs simultaneously. Evaluated against state-of-the-art open-source and commercial systems under simulated real-world conditions, SMIA achieves up to 100% ASR against standalone CMs, 97.5% against VASs, and 82% against combined CM and VAS pipelines, conclusively outperforming prior work and underscoring the need for dynamic, adaptive defenses.

items.title: BiSASV: Bidirectional Feature Modulation with Dual-Granularity Fusion for Spoofing-Robust ASV
items.authors: Yiqun Zhou(Tianjin University); Kong Aik Lee(The Hong Kong Polytechnic University); Ji Liu(Tianjin University); Longbiao Wang(Tianjin University; Huiyan Technology (Tianjin) Co., Ltd)
items.abstract: Automatic speaker verification (ASV) systems are vulnerable to synthetic speech attacks. However, existing feature-level fusion for spoofing-robust ASV (SASV) generally relies on unidirectional CM-to-ASV interactions, ignoring speaker context. We propose BiSASV, a bidirectional modulation spoofing-robust automatic speaker verification system that establishes a reciprocal information flow between the ASV and countermeasure (CM) subsystems. A bidirectional modulation network is introduced to inject global speaker context into the CM, while the enhanced CM features inversely gate the ASV embeddings. Furthermore, a dual-granularity fusion strategy is explored to capture both fine-grained and global discriminative cues. Experimental results show that the proposed system yields an SASV equal error rate (SASV-EER) of 0.73% and a minimum agnostic detection cost function (min a-DCF) of 0.0153 on the ASVspoof 2019 LA set, significantly outperforming unidirectional baseline methods.

items.title: AGENT: A Black-box Adversarial Attack Exposing the Achilles' Heel of SASV Systems
items.authors: Yowon Lee(Soongsil University); Seongkyu Han(Soongsil University); Thien-Phuc Doan(Soongsil University); Souhwan Jung(Soongsil University)
items.abstract: Spoofing-Aware Speaker Verification (SASV) enhances Automatic Speaker Verification (ASV) by integrating countermeasure (CM) modules to defend against spoofing attacks. Recent studies show that SASV improves robustness against both spoofing and adversarial attacks on standalone ASV. However, attacks targeting the full ASV-CM pipeline remain underexplored. We propose AGENT, a black-box adversarial attack that jointly deceives both ASV and CM modules. AGENT is built upon two key designs: (1) a score-maximization objective that amplifies ASV confidence beyond decision margins, and (2) a directional-selective gradient fusion strategy that explicitly resolves gradient conflicts between modules. Experiments demonstrate that AGENT achieves up to 99.62% Attack Success Rate (ASR) across diverse SASV architectures. These results reveal critical vulnerabilities in current SASV systems and highlight the need for stronger defenses in real-world voice authentication systems.

title: Acoustic Event Detection 1
header: Tuesday 29 September 2026 - 09:00-11:00 - Area 5 - Oral 8 - Acoustic Event Detection 1

items.title: Mind the Gap: Detecting Cluster Exits for Robust Local Density-Based Score Normalization in Anomalous Sound Detection
items.authors: Kevin Wilkinghoff(Aalborg University; Pioneer Centre for AI); Gordon Wichern(Mitsubishi Electric Research Laboratories); Jonathan Le Roux(Mitsubishi Electric Research Laboratories); Zheng-Hua Tan(Aalborg University; Pioneer Centre for AI)
items.abstract: Local density-based score normalization is an effective component of distance-based embedding methods for anomalous sound detection, particularly when data densities vary across conditions or domains. In practice, however, performance depends strongly on neighborhood size. Increasing it can degrade detection accuracy when neighborhood expansion crosses cluster boundaries, violating the locality assumption of local density estimation. This observation motivates adapting the neighborhood size based on locality preservation rather than fixing it in advance. We realize this by proposing cluster exit detection, a lightweight mechanism that identifies distance discontinuities and selects neighborhood sizes accordingly. Experiments across multiple embedding models and datasets show improved robustness to neighborhood-size selection and consistent performance gains.

items.title: Lung-SRAD: Spectral-Aware Regularized Audio DASS with Dual-Axis Patch-Mix Contrastive Learning for Respiratory Sound Classification
items.authors: Hemansh Shridhar(RSC LAB, MODULABS); Miika Toikkanen(RSC LAB, MODULABS); June-Woo Kim(Department of Electronic Engineering, Wonkwang University)
items.abstract: Recent respiratory sound classification (RSC) studies largely rely on CLS-token driven self-attention architectures such as the Audio Spectrogram Transformer (AST). While effective at modeling global context, recent analyses suggest a low-pass filtering behavior that may reduce sensitivity to localized abnormal patterns. In this work, we investigate State Space Models (SSMs) as an alternative backbone for RSC. Using the Distilled Audio State Space model, we analyze intermediate representations through spectral response curves and observe stronger preservation of mid-to-high spatial-frequency components. Based on these observations, we introduce spectral-aware layer regularization using Gaussian convolution applied to selected layers. We further propose Dual-Axis Patch-Mix contrastive learning tailored to SSM-based audio models for robust representation learning. Experiments on the ICBHI benchmark show that our approach achieves 64.48% score, outperforming the AST baseline by 5%. Code is available at https://github.com/RSC-Toolkit/Lung-SRAD.

items.title: TriA Pipeline: A Large-Scale Automatic Audio Annotation Pipeline For Audio Classification In Specific Scenarios
items.authors: Hong Lyu(South China University of Technology); Mingru Yang(South China University of Technology); Qianhua He(South China University of Technology); Yanxiong Li(South China University of Technology); Jinxin Huang(South China University of Technology); Zhengyu Pei(South China University of Technology)
items.abstract: There are some datasets of varying scales for audio classification (AC) applied to different tasks. However, annotated data is limited for most scenarios, such as domestic environments. To address this challenge, we propose an Automatic Audio Annotation Pipeline -TriA Pipeline, which can efficiently convert audio from various scenarios into high-quality training data with audio event annotations. A TriA dataset was constructed with the TriA Pipeline, over 2130 hours of audio covering 431 audio classes. Furthermore, we partitioned a prior-knowledge-guided subset (TriAGK) from TriA and conduct comparative experiments on three domestic AC tasks. Comparing the result on manually annotated data only and that on manually annotated data combines TriAGK, TriAGK could achieve average relative gains of 3.97% in accuracy and 3.35% in Macro-F1, validating the effectiveness of TriAGK and the TriA Pipeline.

items.title: Acoustic Landmark Detector based on Conformer and HuBERT
items.authors: Mateo Cámara(Universidad Politécnica de Madrid; MIT); José Luis Blanco(Universidad Politécnica de Madrid); Juan Ignacio Godino-Llorente(Universidad Politécnica de Madrid); Jeung-Yoon Choi(MIT); Stefanie Shattuck-Hufnagel(MIT)
items.abstract: Acoustic landmarks (abrupt acoustic changes tied to speech events) offer a linguistically grounded representation for speech analysis. We study automatic landmark detection with Conformer models, evaluating 14 configurations spanning architecture, loss, label representation, feature extractor, and data conditions on 1,839 manually annotated utterances with eight landmark types. We propose Gaussian soft labels with per-class temporal spread (σ=10-20 ms), improving F1@20 ms by 7.0% absolute vs. hard labels by modeling annotation variability. Frozen HuBERT features perform best without fine-tuning (F1@20 ms=0.77). Stops and fricatives are reliable (F1>0.80), while vowels remain challenging (F1≈0.55). On our corpus, our system reaches a 13.8% Landmark Error Rate (LER). This is not directly comparable to AutoLandmark (31.3%) or SpeechMark (56.5%), evaluated on a different corpus and metric. Per-class trends show detectability increases with event abruptness, consistent with Stevens' theory.

items.title: Ecologically-Constrained Task Arithmetic for Multi-Taxa Bioacoustic Classifiers Without Shared Data
items.authors: Ragib Amin Nihal(Institute of Science Tokyo); Benjamin Yen(Institute of Science Tokyo; RIKEN BDR); Runwu Shi(Institute of Science Tokyo); Takeshi Ashizawa(Institute of Science Tokyo); Kazuhiro Nakadai(Institute of Science Tokyo)
items.abstract: Training data for bioacoustics is scattered across taxa, regions, and institutions. Centralizing it all is often infeasible. We show that independently fine-tuned BEATs encoders can be composed into a unified 661-species classifier via task vector arithmetic without sharing data. We find that bioacoustic task vectors are near-orthogonal (cosine 0.01-0.09). Their separation aligns closely with spectral distribution distance, a gradient consistent with the acoustic niche hypothesis. This geometry makes simple averaging optimal while sign-conflict methods reduce accuracy by one to six percentage points. Composition also creates an asymmetric gap: species-rich groups lose accuracy relative to joint training while underrepresented taxa gain, a redistribution useful for equitable biodiversity monitoring. We verify linear mode connectivity across all taxonomic pairs, demonstrate zero-shot transfer to new regions, and identify domain negation as a boundary condition where composition fails. These results enable a collaborative paradigm for bioacoustics where institutions share only task vectors to assemble multi-taxa classifiers, preserving data privacy.

items.title: Beyond task performance: Decoding bioacoustic embeddings with speech features
items.authors: Ines Nolasco(Earth Species Project); Jules Cauzinille(Earth Species Project); Marius Miron(Earth Species Project); Gagan Narula(Earth Species Project); Milad Alizadeh(Earth Species Project); Emmanuel Fernandez(Earth Species Project); Matthieu Geist(Earth Species Project); Ellen Gilsenan-McMahon(Earth Species Project); Olivier Pietquin(Earth Species Project); Emmanuel Chemla(Earth Species Project); Sara Keen(Earth Species Project)
items.abstract: Pretrained audio embeddings are standard in bioacoustics, yet little is known about which acoustic features they encode, nor which are useful for a given task. This limits transparency and extension to rare species or data-scarce domains. We ask which speech-like features bioacoustic embeddings encode, framing evaluation as interpretability rather than benchmarking. Using the 88 eGeMAPS features across six taxonomic groups, we apply linear and nonlinear regression probes to quantify which acoustic properties each model captures. Results confirm a "no free lunch" pattern: no single model captures the full feature space, while a concatenated embedding performs best, suggesting complementary coverage. Loudness is best encoded (R² = 0.76) while F0 is hardest to recover (R² = 0.33). Cross-referencing recoverability with per-species feature salience (NMI) offers data-driven hypotheses for model selection in bioacoustics.

title: Language-Model and Codec-Token Speech Enhancement
header: Tuesday 29 September 2026 - 09:00-11:00 - Area 6 - Oral 2 - Language-Model and Codec-Token Speech Enhancement

items.title: UniSE: A Unified Framework for Decoder-Only Autoregressive LM-Based Speech Enhancement
items.authors: Haoyin Yan(Alibaba); Chengwei Liu(Alibaba); Shaofei Xue(Alibaba); Xiaotao Liang(Alibaba); Yinghao Liu(Alibaba); Yuxiang Kong(Alibaba); Zheng Xue(Alibaba)
items.abstract: Neural audio codecs have largely promoted the application of language models (LMs) for speech applications. However, the effectiveness of autoregressive LM-based models in unifying speech enhancement (SE) tasks remains underexplored. In this work, we propose UniSE, a unified decoder-only LM-based framework to handle different SE tasks including speech restoration, target speaker extraction, and speech separation. Conditioned on input speech features, it autoregressively generates target discrete tokens, facilitating compatibility between distinct learning patterns of multiple tasks. To further optimize speech quality, we introduce a progressive reinforcement learning strategy with multiple assessment criteria. Experiments on several benchmarks show that UniSE achieves competitive performance compared to discriminative and generative baselines, demonstrating the capacity of LMs in unifying SE tasks. The code and demo is available at: https://github.com/alibaba/unified-audio/tree/main/QuarkAudio-UniSE.

items.title: DelayGSE: A Generative Speech Enhancement Framework with Delayed Text-Aware Conditioning
items.authors: Xin Yuan(Guangzhou Shiyuan Electronic Technology); Junling Lv(Guangzhou Shiyuan Electronic Technology); Zezhou Xu(SUFE); Xingjun Tan(Guangzhou Shiyuan Electronic Technology); Liangliang Li(Guangzhou Shiyuan Electronic Technology); Yanqiang Lei(Guangzhou Shiyuan Electronic Technology)
items.abstract: Recent generative speech enhancement methods based on language and diffusion models achieve strong perceptual quality but are more susceptible than discriminative approaches to speech-like hallucinations under low SNRs and transient noise. We propose DelayGSE, a text-aware generative speech enhancement framework built on a multi-codebook language model for denoising, dereverberation, and audio super-resolution. DelayGSE conditions on noisy-speech STFT features and Whisper encoder representations, and models multiple discrete codebooks in a delayed manner to stabilize generation. A text-aware mechanism suppresses hallucinations, while an importance-aware codebook weighting strategy balances perceptual fidelity and semantic consistency. Experiments demonstrate state-of-the-art performance, with ablations showing effective hallucination suppression and a 15.8% relative word error rate reduction. Audio samples are available at https://delaygse.github.io/.

items.title: StuPASE: Towards Low-Hallucination Studio-Quality Generative Speech Enhancement
items.authors: Xiaobin Rong(Nanjing University; Cisco Systems, Inc.); Jun Gao(Nanjing University); Zheng Wang(Nanjing University; Horizon Robotics); Mansur Yesilbursa(Cisco Systems, Inc.); Kamil Wojcicki(Cisco Systems, Inc.); Jing Lu(Nanjing University; Horizon Robotics)
items.abstract: Achieving high perceptual quality without hallucination remains a challenge in generative speech enhancement (SE). A representative approach, PASE, is robust to hallucination but has limited perceptual quality under adverse conditions. We propose StuPASE, built upon PASE to achieve studio-level quality while retaining its low-hallucination property. First, we show that finetuning PASE with dry targets rather than targets containing simulated early reflections substantially improves dereverberation. Second, to address performance limitations under strong additive noise, we replace the GAN-based generative module in PASE with a flow-matching module, enabling studio-quality generation even under highly challenging conditions. Experiments demonstrate that StuPASE consistently produces perceptually high-quality speech while maintaining low hallucination, outperforming state-of-the-art SE methods. Audio demos are available at: https://xiaobin-rong.github.io/stupase_demo/.

items.title: Improving DF-Conformer using Hydra for high-fidelity generative speech enhancement on discrete codec token
items.authors: Shogo Seki(CyberAgent, Inc.); Shaoxiang Dang(CyberAgent, Inc.); Li Li(CyberAgent, Inc.)
items.abstract: The Dilated FAVOR Conformer (DF-Conformer) is an efficient variant of the Conformer architecture designed for speech enhancement (SE). It employs fast attention through positive orthogonal random features (FAVOR+) to mitigate the quadratic complexity associated with self-attention, while utilizing dilated convolution to expand the receptive field. This combination results in impressive performance across various SE models. In this paper, we propose replacing FAVOR+ with bidirectional selective structured state-space sequence models to achieve two main objectives: (1) enhancing global sequential modeling by eliminating the approximations inherent in FAVOR+, and (2) maintaining linear complexity relative to the sequence length. Specifically, we utilize Hydra, a bidirectional extension of Mamba, framed within the structured matrix mixer framework. Experiments conducted using a generative SE model on discrete codec tokens, known as Genhancer, demonstrate that the proposed method surpasses the performance of the DF-Conformer.

items.title: Towards Robust Generative Speech Enhancement Using Vector Quantisation-Based Neural Audio Codec
items.authors: Haixin Zhao(Ghent University - imec); Nilesh Madhu(Ghent University - imec)
items.abstract: This work investigates modelling strategies in continuous and discrete latent spaces in the vector quantisation (VQ)-based neural audio codec (NAC) speech enhancement (SE), along with the role of VQ regularisation. We propose cNAC-SE and dNAC-SE frameworks that predict continuous representations and discrete tokens in latent space, respectively. Theoretical analysis and visualisations in latent space are performed to exhibit their inherent modelling mechanisms. Experimental results show that the fully fine-tuned cNAC-SE model consistently outperforms all dNAC-SE variants across diverse test conditions and achieves leading performance among established generative approaches in DNS-MOS metrics. Comparison with the discriminative counterpart shows that VQ enhances robustness through an intrinsic effect of clean-prior-constrained regularisation, independent of discrete token processing. This highlights the transferable value of VQ regularisation to other continuous modelling methods.

items.title: Post-Training Speech Enhancement Language Models with Perceptual Rewards
items.authors: Frédéric Berdoȥ(ETH Zürich); Luca A. Lanzendöerfer(ETH Zürich); Antonis Asonitis(ETH Zürich); Roger Wattenhofer(ETH Zürich)
items.abstract: Speech enhancement language models achieve strong results when trained on discrete audio tokens, but their optimization relies on token-level cross-entropy rather than the perceptual metrics used for evaluation. We introduce a post-training stage for autoregressive speech enhancement language models using Group Sequence Policy Optimization (GSPO) with multi-metric perceptual rewards. Our method directly optimizes non-differentiable quality metrics (DNSMOS, WER, and UTMOS) as reward signals, without learned surrogates or offline preference pairs. Applied to two autoregressive base models, UniSE and GenSE, our approach achieves state-of-the-art results on the DNS2020 benchmark. A human evaluation ablation further shows that the composite multi-metric reward is preferred over any single-metric variant, confirming that multi-reward optimization avoids the reward hacking observed with single-metric training.

title: Controllable and Expressive Speech Synthesis
header: Tuesday 29 September 2026 - 09:00-11:00 - Area 7 - Oral 8 - Controllable and Expressive Speech Synthesis

items.title: Learnable Classifier-Free Guidance Null Embeddings for Enhanced Controllable Speech Synthesis
items.authors: Biel Tura-Vecino(Cantina Labs); Yoach Lacombe(Cantina Labs); Julian Weber(Cantina Labs); Zbigniew Latka(Cantina Labs); Haitong Zhang(Cantina Labs); Logan Hart(Cantina Labs); Eren Golge(Cantina Labs)
items.abstract: Classifier-free Guidance (CFG) is widely adopted in text-to-speech (TTS) systems to enhance generation quality and conditioning fidelity by interpolating between conditioned and unconditioned predictions. A common unconditional technique is to use an empty representation, in the form of a fixed null vector. In this work, we propose replacing this representation with a learnable unconditional embedding, optimized to represent a meaningful unconditional state. Objective and subjective evaluations demonstrate that learnable null embeddings consistently outperform fixed null embeddings across speaker similarity, speech stability, and expressiveness, while exhibiting greater robustness to larger guidance scales. We further show that learning a distinct unconditional embedding for each of the TTS conditioning modalities allows fine-grained control over speaker and text guidance, showcasing the trade-off between similarity and quality, and stability and expressiveness in the generated speech.

items.title: Synthesizing the Lombard Effect: Multi-Level Control of Speech Clarity and Vocal Effort in TTS
items.authors: Seymanur Akti(KIT; KCT); Alexander Waibel(KIT; CMU)
items.abstract: Humans tend to speak louder and clearer in challenging environments, such as noisy conditions or when addressing hearing-impaired listeners, which is called Lombard effect. To simulate this behavior in speech synthesis systems, we introduce a flow-matching based text-to-speech (TTS) model trained with vocal effort and articulation pseudo-labels. The proposed model achieves continuous and disentangled control of vocal effort and articulation, while also enabling word-level emphasis for clarifying specific segments of an utterance. Experimental results show that these control mechanisms effectively improve clarity-related acoustic features. Furthermore, speech-in-noise experiments demonstrate that our model successfully simulates the intelligibility gains of human clear speech in noisy conditions.

items.title: CrossAccent-TTS: Cross-Lingual Accent-Intensity Controllable Text-to-Speech via Disentangled Speaker and Accent Representations
items.authors: Ram Annamdevula(Sony Research India); Ankit Tatawat(Sony Research India); Ashishkumar P. Gudmalwar(Sony Research India); Nirmesh J. Shah(Sony Research India); Pankaj Wasnik(Sony Research India)
items.abstract: Accent conversion and controllability remain fundamental challenges in cross-lingual text-to-speech (TTS), particularly for low-resource and phonetically diverse Indic languages. While recent large language model (LLM)-based TTS systems exhibit strong cross-lingual generalization, they provide limited explicit control over accent characteristics and intensity. In this paper, we propose CrossAccentTTS, a framework that enables both accent control and conversion while preserving speaker identity. Specifically, we introduce an Accent Intensity Controller (AIC) that injects weighted language embeddings into the accent subspace, allowing smooth interpolation between accents and fine-grained modulation of accent strength at inference time. Experiments on the Indic Multilingual and L2-arctic datasets shows that CrossAccent-TTS achieves precise control of accent intensity, outperforming strong baselines in accent similarity and controllability by maintaining speaker similarity and naturalness.

items.title: CtrlSpeech: Coarse-to-Fine Control for Expressive Speech Synthesis
items.authors: Zhisheng Zheng(The University of Texas at Austin); Xiaohang Sun(Amazon); Zhu Liu(Amazon); Caren Chen(Amazon); Rohith Kumar(Amazon); Manoj Aggarwal(Amazon); Gerard Medioni(Amazon); David Harwath(The University of Texas at Austin)
items.abstract: Recent Text-To-Speech (TTS) systems have achieved strong naturalness and zero-shot voice cloning performance, but fine-grained control of expressive speech at the word or phoneme level remains challenging. We propose CTRLSPEECH, a controllable, expressive TTS framework with coarse-to-fine control. Built on the DiTAR architecture, CTRLSPEECH combines global speaker conditioning with phone-aligned pitch, loudness, and duration signals, enabling localized prosodic control while preserving the target speaker's timbre. This design allows users to adjust expressive attributes at a fine temporal granularity, making speech refinement more flexible and controllable. Experimental results show that CTRLSPEECH achieves competitive zero-shot TTS performance and improves controllability over expressive attributes, demonstrating its effectiveness for flexible and practical expressive speech synthesis. Our demo, code and model weights are available at CTRLSPEECH.

items.title: ProsoCodec: Prosody-Oriented Speech Codec for Voice Conversion
items.authors: Jeongsoo Choi(KAIST); Ji-Hoon Kim(Chung-Ang University); Shujie Hu(The Chinese University of Hong Kong); Joon Son Chung(KAIST)
items.abstract: Neural speech codecs efficiently compress speech and have become a foundation for speech generation, but they are typically learned as holistic representations that intertwine linguistic content, speaker identity, and prosody. While this design is effective for zero-shot voice cloning, it hinders downstream tasks that require prosody preservation or transfer, such as voice conversion. To address this, we introduce ProsoCodec, a prosody-oriented speech codec that models prosody as a conditional residual rather than as a disentangled stream. Specifically, by conditioning both the encoder and decoder on text and speaker embeddings as prefix tokens, the discrete bottleneck is encouraged to capture prosodic variation not explained by content and speaker. To further preserve prosody, we use the low-frequency mel band and train the model on paired same-speaker utterances. Experiments on voice conversion show improved prosody preservation and reduced source-timbre leakage.

items.title: LibriTTS-VI: A Public Corpus and Novel Methods for Efficient Voice Impression Control
items.authors: Junki Ohmura(Sony Group Corporation); Yuki Ito(Sony Group Corporation); Emiru Tsunoo(Sony Group Corporation); Toshiyuki Sekiya(Sony Group Corporation); Toshiyuki Kumakura(Sony Group Corporation)
items.abstract: Numerical voice impression (VI) control (e.g., scaling brightness) enables fine-grained control in text-to-speech (TTS). However, it faces two challenges: no public corpus and impression leakage, where reference audio biases synthesized voice away from the target VI. To address the first challenge, we introduce LibriTTS-VI, the first public VI corpus built on LibriTTSR. For the second, we hypothesize a single reference causes leakage by entangling speaker identity and VI. To mitigate this, we propose 1) disentangled training with two utterances from the same speaker for speaker and VI conditioning, and 2) a reference-free method controlling the impression solely via target VI. Experimentally, our best method improves controllability: 11-dimensional VI mean squared error drops from 0.61 to 0.41 objectively and 1.15 to 0.92 subjectively. A comparison with a prompt-based TTS reveals imprecise numerical control and entanglement between VI and text semantics, which our methods overcome.

title: Resource Constrained Speech Recognition
header: Tuesday 29 September 2026 - 09:00-11:00 - Area 9 - Oral 3 - Resource Constrained Speech Recognition

items.title: Not All Frames Are Equal: Difference-Aware Quantization for Ultra-Low-Bit ASR
items.authors: Woori Jeon(Sogang University); Jungmin So(Sogang University)
items.abstract: Post-training quantization (PTQ) methods such as GPTQ and AWQ compress large language models effectively, but applying them to automatic speech recognition (ASR) at ultra-low bit-widths (2-3 bits) causes severe transcription degradation. Unlike discrete text tokens, speech activations are highly correlated in steady-state and zero-padded regions yet change rapidly at phonetic boundaries; when all frames contribute equally to the Hessian, static frames dominate calibration and obscure informative transitions. We propose DiffAQ, which computes frame-to-frame activation differences to measure the rate of acoustic change and assigns Hessian importance proportionally, concentrating quantization precision on phonetically critical frames. As a training-free modification to GPTQ, DiffAQ consistently reduces WER across various Whisper sizes and standard benchmarks, with the largest gains at 2-bit precision where baseline methods frequently produce degenerate outputs.
